blocks.text: Most of an AI assistant's value for a policy analyst comes down to three jobs: reading fast, finding the right source, and turning notes into a clear brief. Lazur works through your voice and your screen. You hold ⌥ ⌘, ask about whatever is open, and it answers out loud. It can point at the paragraph you mean, draft a reply, or send a research job to Chrome while you keep working.
What an AI assistant for policy analysts does on a Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in the notch at the top of your screen. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Read your employer's rules before you rely on that in government or think tank work.

Lazur does four things for this job. It explains what is on screen, out loud. It points at things, drawing a circle and a label around them. It guides you through a menu one click at a time, waiting for each click. It drafts and types text, and it sends research jobs to its own Chrome tabs. Those jobs come back with a summary and a report. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you.

Think of it as a sharp colleague sitting beside you, not a plugin inside Word or PowerPoint. That difference shapes how you use it. You stay in charge of the document. Lazur answers, shows and types. You decide what goes into the brief.
Where a policy analyst's day actually goes

No study measures how policy analysts spend their computer time, so start with knowledge-work data. Across Microsoft 365 apps, the average worker spent 57% of time communicating in meetings, email and chat. Creating documents, spreadsheets and presentations took 43%. Email alone took about 15%. The survey covered about 31,000 full-time workers in 31 markets, with usage data from the 28 days ending March 2023.

Your own week may tilt harder one way. Use the split as a starting point. A simple tally on paper tells you more than any average does. Write down each block of the day for five working days, then sort it into messages, reading, writing and searching.

The heaviest email users feel the squeeze most. The top quarter of users spend 8.8 hours a week on email, according to the same study. That is a top-quartile figure, not an average, so don't use it as your baseline. Treat it as a warning if your inbox stays open all day.

Microsoft's 2025 follow-up adds pace. The average worker receives 117 emails a day, and most are skimmed in under 60 seconds. The average worker also receives 153 Teams messages per weekday. Microsoft 365 users are interrupted about every 2 minutes by a meeting, email or notification. Each interruption pulls you out of the paragraph you were reading.

Searching is the last big slice. Atlassian's State of Teams 2025 survey, which included 12,000 knowledge workers and 200 executives, found that leaders and teams waste 25% of their time searching for answers. The figures are self-reported, and the survey does not define searching tightly. Still, anyone who has hunted for last year's figure in a shared drive will recognize the problem.
Where these numbers come from and what they cannot tell you

These are knowledge-worker numbers, not policy analyst numbers. Microsoft's 2023 and 2025 studies use different methods. The 2025 page also contradicts itself on a few details, such as the share of meetings that are ad hoc. Treat the figures as the shape of the problem, not a measure of your week.

The closest official occupation is political scientists. The Bureau of Labor Statistics has no entry for policy analysts. Its handbook gives a median pay of $142,080 per year based on May 2025 data, with about 6,100 jobs in 2025. It projects employment to change by minus 2% from 2025 to 2035. Use it as a proxy only, and check the role you are actually applying for.
Reading long reports without losing the afternoon

A consultation response or a long evaluation rarely needs a full read on the first pass. You need the findings, the method and the caveats. Lazur helps you reach those fast, but it works on what is open and what you ask. Open the document first, then hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask something specific.
Here is a worked example. You open an evaluation of a housing subsidy scheme and need its main caveats before a midday meeting. Follow these steps.

items: Open the PDF in Preview or Chrome, then scroll to the summary section.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask: What are the main caveats the authors give?
Listen to the answer, then ask a follow up: Which page says that?
Ask Lazur to point at the sentence. It draws a circle and a label so you can check the original.
Copy the lines you need with ⌘C, then write your own summary in Word.

blocks.text: Scanned PDFs cause trouble for any reader. If you cannot select the text, the page is an image. Lazur reads what is on screen, so a blurry scan can give a weak answer. Look for a text version from the publisher, or read the table yourself.
The most common mistake is asking for a summary and pasting it straight into a brief. A summary is a starting point. Ask for the page, then read the page.

blocks.title: Check every figure
blocks.text: A summary can drop a qualifier, flip a comparison or round a number. Before a figure goes into a brief, open the original and read the sentence around it.
Finding the source behind a number

Policy writing runs on sourced numbers. A line that says a scheme reached a share of households needs a source, a year and a definition. Lazur helps you trace that trail. Hold ⌥ ⌘ on the sentence and ask where the figure comes from. If the source is on screen, Lazur can point at it.

If the source is not open, send a research job. Ask Lazur to find the survey and summarize its method. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and comes back with a summary and a report. Treat those as leads. Open the page, find the table, check the year and the sample, then cite the original.

items: Find the sentence in the original, not in a summary.
Note the year the data was collected.
Check the sample, the population and the definition used.
Confirm the unit, such as percent of households or percent of respondents.
Save the link next to the figure in your notes.

blocks.text: Sources also change. If a brief goes out a month later, check the publisher page again before you send. Lazur can help you find the newest version, but the date on the page is your evidence.
Writing briefs, memos and decks in Word and PowerPoint

Creating takes 43% of the average worker's Microsoft 365 time in the 2023 study. For you that often means a brief due Friday, a memo for a minister's office and a deck for a committee. Each has its own structure. Each still needs the same numbers, sourced the same way.

In Word, the work is structure. Use heading styles, add page numbers and turn on track changes when a colleague marks up the draft. Lazur can explain where a setting lives, then guide you through it one click at a time. The [Word guide for policy analysts](/for/policy-analysts/word) covers the menus that matter most.

Current Office for Mac is version 16.114.3, released October 27, 2026. Menus move between versions, so if a path in an old guide looks different, say so out loud. Ask Lazur to point at the button you can see, rather than trusting a screenshot from last year.

blocks.text: Comparing two drafts before a sign-off is a common task. The steps are in our [guide to comparing two documents in Word](/how-to/compare-two-documents-in-word). Ask Lazur to guide you through Review > Compare. It waits for each click, so you stay in control of the file.

For decks, the work is pacing and speaker notes. Lazur can explain what is on the current slide and draft speaker notes in your words. For slide numbers, see the [slide numbers guide](/how-to/add-slide-numbers-in-powerpoint). The [PowerPoint guide for policy analysts](/for/policy-analysts/powerpoint) covers briefing decks in more detail.
Email and the inbox you cannot clear

Email is where most of the 117 daily messages land. Most of them need a yes, a no or a forward. The best use of an assistant here is triage. Ask Lazur what a message wants from you, then ask it to draft the reply. You read the draft, change any commitments, and send it yourself.

Apple Mail is the built-in choice for many Mac users. Add an email account first, such as iCloud, Exchange or Gmail. You can attach photos and documents, reply to the sender or reply to all, and search by keyword with filters such as sender or subject. Apple's guide covers macOS Sonoma 14 through macOS 27 in its version selector.

If your office uses Outlook, check the version first. Classic Outlook for Mac is gone for Microsoft 365 subscribers. Subscribers could not switch back to the classic client from build 16.102 in mid-October 2025. The new Outlook is now the default. Enterprise customers were scheduled to move in April 2026, and admins can still switch back. Ask IT before you change anything.

Outlook changes reach the calendar too. Version 16.114, released October 14, 2026, lets Microsoft 365 apps appear in the Outlook left rail. It also lets you choose a third-party meeting provider when you create a calendar event. Ask Lazur to point at those options if you cannot find them.
Confidential and personal data in government and think tank work

Policy work often touches personal data, draft legislation or material marked confidential. Your employer decides what can go into an AI tool. Follow those rules before you hold the key. If your office has no rule yet, ask before you paste a draft, an interview transcript or a file with names in it.

Lazur sends audio and screenshots to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models. Those are Lazur's own practices, and they do not replace your office's policy. This page does not claim any compliance certification for Lazur. Check with your data protection lead before you use it on sensitive files.
A practical rule helps. Use Lazur on public documents and your own notes first. Hold off on anything with personal data until your employer confirms the rules.
A realistic day with Lazur

The sample day below shows how the work splits. Morning starts with triage, so the inbox stops setting your agenda. Late morning goes to a research job while you read the first source. Early afternoon is for figures and comparing drafts. Late afternoon ends with a reminder, not a last-minute scramble.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant on policy work

items: Asking for a summary, then pasting it into a brief without opening the source.
Trusting a figure that has no year, sample or definition attached.
Letting the assistant write the whole memo. Your name goes on the judgment, not the tool.
Treating research results as verified facts instead of leads to check.
Following a menu path from an old guide without checking your Office for Mac version.
Pasting confidential or personal data before checking your employer's rules.

blocks.text: How to set up Lazur on your Mac

items: Download Lazur from the [download page](/download) and open it. The trial starts when you first open the app, and no credit card is needed.
Allow the microphone and screen access that macOS asks for. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about the open document. Start simple, such as: What is this page about?
Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in Word, Mail or Chrome. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.
Read every draft before you use it. Edit it, check every figure, and send it yourself.

blocks.text: Start with one document and one question. A narrow start teaches you what Lazur can see and what it cannot. When you are ready, check the [pricing page](/pricing) for current plans.
What Lazur does not do for you

Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It is not a plugin or add-in for Word, PowerPoint or Mail, and it has no partnership with any app maker. When it guides you through a menu, you do the clicking. That feels slow at first, then you learn the menus you use most.
It also cannot judge the evidence for you. It can explain what a paragraph says and where it sits. Whether the evidence holds is still your call, and so is the recommendation that follows from it.
Pricing and where to start

Lazur starts with a Pro trial that begins when you first open the app, with no credit card. After the trial, Pro and Power plans are billed monthly or annually. Dictation is unlimited on both plans. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for current amounts, since plans can change.
Pick one job for your first week. Triage your inbox on Monday, check one source on Wednesday, and draft one brief by Friday. Those steps show more than any feature list does.

faq.question: What is an AI assistant for policy analysts?
faq.answer: It is a tool that helps with reading, research and writing while you work. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. You hold ⌥ ⌘, ask about what is on screen, and it answers out loud.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Word or PowerPoint files?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It explains, points, guides you one click at a time, and drafts text you can paste or dictate.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Outlook and Apple Mail?
faq.answer: Lazur works on what is on your screen, so it can help with messages open in Mail or Outlook. It is not an add-in for either app, and it has no partnership with any app maker.

faq.question: Is my data safe with an AI assistant?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Follow your employer's rules on confidential and personal data first.

faq.question: Should I trust a summary from an AI tool?
faq.answer: Not without checking. A summary can drop a caveat or round a number. Open the original, find the sentence, and confirm the year and the sample before you cite it.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is for macOS on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.

faq.question: What if my office still uses classic Outlook?
faq.answer: Classic Outlook for Mac is no longer an option for Microsoft 365 subscribers, since build 16.102 in mid-October 2025. Check with IT before you change your setup.

faq.question: Is there a trial before I pay?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur starts with a Pro trial that begins when you first open the app, with no credit card. Check the pricing page for current plans after the trial.
